items.followUp: State Archimedes’ principle and name the force exerted by the fluid on an immersed object.

rubric.why: Identifies the upward force on an immersed body.
rubric.description: Names the upward force (buoyant force or upthrust).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the force as an upward buoyant force or upthrust.

accept: equal to the weight of the displaced fluid
rubric.why: States the defining equality in Archimedes’ principle.
rubric.description: States that the upward force equals the weight of the fluid displaced.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the equality with the displaced fluid’s weight.

modelAnswer: An object wholly or partially immersed in a fluid experiences an upward force called upthrust or buoyant force.
This force is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the object.

items.followUp: Using a speed-time graph, derive the relation v_f² − v_i² = 2as.

rubric.why: Uses the area under the speed-time graph to obtain displacement.
rubric.description: Writes displacement as the area of the trapezium under the graph.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the trapezium-area relation or its equivalent.

rubric.why: Relates acceleration to the change in speed over time.
rubric.description: Writes the acceleration relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a=(v_f−v_i)/t or its rearrangement.

rubric.why: Combines the displacement and acceleration relations correctly.
rubric.description: Substitutes to obtain the product of the sum and difference of the speeds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct substitution and product.

rubric.why: Uses the difference-of-squares identity to reach the required result.
rubric.description: Obtains the required relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the final relation.

modelAnswer: Displacement s is the area under the speed-time graph: s = 1/2 (v_i + v_f)t.
Acceleration a = (v_f − v_i)/t, so at = v_f − v_i.
Therefore, 2as = 2 × 1/2 (v_i + v_f)t × a = (v_i + v_f)at.
Substituting at = v_f − v_i: 2as = (v_i + v_f)(v_f − v_i) = v_f² − v_i².

items.followUp: A body weighs 30 N. Find the upward force required to give it an upward acceleration of 3 m s⁻². Take g = 10 m s⁻².

rubric.why: Identifies the given weight.
rubric.description: Records the body’s weight as 20 N.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying W = 20 N.

rubric.why: Uses W = mg to find the mass; g = 10 m s⁻² is commonly used for this board-level calculation.
rubric.description: Calculates the body’s mass from its weight.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct mass using the stated or standard value of g.

rubric.why: Applies Newton’s second law to the upward resultant force.
rubric.description: Sets the net upward force equal to ma.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct force equation.

rubric.why: Accounts for both the weight downward and the required resultant force upward.
rubric.description: Rearranges the force equation to find the applied upward force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for adding the weight and ma, with appropriate substitution.

rubric.why: Gives the required applied force with units.
rubric.description: States the final upward force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct final force with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: W = 20 N, a = 2 m s⁻², and take g = 10 m s⁻².
Using W = mg, m = W/g = 20 N ÷ 10 m s⁻² = 2 kg.
For upward motion, F − W = ma.
Therefore, F = W + ma = 20 N + (2 kg)(2 m s⁻²).
F = 24 N upward.

items.followUp: Define centre of gravity and describe how to find the centre of gravity of an irregular cardboard shape.

accept: point through which the whole weight acts
point of application of the whole weight
whole weight of a body acts
rubric.why: Gives the defining property of the centre of gravity.
rubric.description: Defines the centre of gravity as the point through which the whole weight of a body acts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: Describes the first suspension and the use of a vertical reference.
rubric.description: Suspends the shape freely and uses a plumb line to mark a vertical line.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the first suspension and plumb-line step.

rubric.why: A second suspension provides another vertical line.
rubric.description: Repeats the suspension from a different point and marks the second vertical line.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a second suspension and line.

rubric.why: The intersection identifies the centre of gravity.
rubric.description: Identifies the intersection of the two vertical lines as the centre of gravity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct location.

modelAnswer: The centre of gravity of a body is the point through which its whole weight may be considered to act.
Suspend the irregular shape freely from a point and hang a plumb line from the same point.
Mark the vertical line indicated by the plumb line on the shape.
Suspend the shape from a second point and mark the second vertical line.
The intersection of the two lines gives the centre of gravity.

items.followUp: What is a micrometer screw gauge, and what is its typical least count?

rubric.why: Identifies the purpose of vernier callipers.
rubric.description: Defines vernier callipers as an instrument for accurate measurement of small lengths or dimensions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable definition or purpose.

rubric.why: Gives the least count of a digital vernier calliper.
rubric.description: States the digital vernier callipers’ least count.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 0.01 mm (equivalent to 0.001 cm).

modelAnswer: Vernier callipers are an instrument used to measure small lengths and dimensions, such as internal or external diameters, accurately.
The least count of digital vernier callipers is 0.01 mm (0.001 cm).

items.followUp: State two rules used to identify significant figures in a measurement.

rubric.why: States the rule for non-zero digits.
rubric.description: All non-zero digits are significant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this rule.

accept: zeros between nonzero digits are significant
rubric.why: States the rule for zeros between non-zero digits.
rubric.description: Zeros between non-zero digits are significant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this rule.

accept: zeros before the first nonzero digit are not significant
rubric.why: States the rule for leading zeros.
rubric.description: Leading zeros are not significant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this rule.

accept: trailing zeros after a decimal are significant
zeros to the right of a decimal are significant
rubric.why: States the rule for trailing zeros in a decimal measurement.
rubric.description: Trailing zeros after a decimal point are significant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this rule.

modelAnswer: All non-zero digits in a measurement are significant.
Zeros between non-zero digits are significant.
Zeros before the first non-zero digit are not significant.
Trailing zeros after a decimal point are significant.

items.followUp: Differentiate between scalar and vector quantities, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: States the defining feature of a scalar quantity.
rubric.description: A scalar has magnitude only.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the scalar distinction.

rubric.why: States the defining feature of a vector quantity.
rubric.description: A vector has both magnitude and direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the vector distinction.

modelAnswer: A scalar quantity has magnitude only; for example, mass or speed.
A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction; for example, force or velocity.

rubric.why: States that the acceleration does not change with time.
rubric.description: Acceleration remains constant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that acceleration is constant.

accept: equal changes in velocity in equal intervals of time
velocity changes by equal amounts in equal time intervals
rubric.why: Explains the meaning of constant acceleration in terms of velocity changes over time.
rubric.description: Velocity changes by equal amounts in equal time intervals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the equal-change/equal-interval condition.

modelAnswer: An object has uniform acceleration when its velocity changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of time.
Thus, its acceleration remains constant.
